Chief_Complaint.content: Patient woke with a severe headache this morning.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: Patient: Um, so I kind of woke up this morning, um, and I've just got this, really horrible pain on the left side of my head. Um, a real kind of headachy feeling.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Headache began upon waking this morning.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: Um, so I kind of woke up this morning, um, and I've just got this, really horrible pain on the left side of my head. Um, a real kind of headachy feeling.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Headache woke the patient at approximately 5:30 AM.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: What, what time did it wake you up?
Patient: Um, probably around, five thirty ish.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Headache is still present at the time of consultation.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: Is the headache still present now?
Patient: Yes, it is.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has had prior headaches but none as severe as the current one.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: Um, I mean uh, I've, had a bit of a history with headaches, but nothing as severe as this before.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Previous headaches were typically frontal and not one-sided.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: Um, not so much on the one side, it tends to be, a bit of a cluster at the front of my head in a way. Um, but this time it's just kind of more prominent on the left side which, I've never really had it, normally they kind of spread across the front of my head.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Current headache is predominantly on the left side.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: ...but this time it's just kind of more prominent on the left side which, I've never really had it...

Doctor: And, um, can I just double-check, do you have any neck stiffness at all?
Patient: Uh, no.

Doctor: OK. And do you have any fever?
Patient: No.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Reports mild sensitivity to bright lights (photophobia).
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: Um, it, I'm a little bit sensitive it just, it kind of, makes my eyes a little bit sore, but nothing that I can't really handle.

Doctor: OK. And, can I just double-check, um, are you feeling nauseous at all?
Patient: Um, not really, like . When I first got up this morning, my head felt a bit dizzy, but that's kind of subsided now, and I, seems to, be fine.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Felt dizzy on getting up this morning, which has since resolved.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: When I first got up this morning, my head felt a bit dizzy, but that's kind of subsided now, and I, seems to, be fine.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Lying down initially makes the head feel sore but then it soothes after a while.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: Um, when I lay down, like, uh, it kind of feels a little bit sore at first, um and it takes me a while to get comfortable. Um, so yeah, at the beginning it does, but then again that's just kind of, um, soothes a little bit.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Overall, headache is better when lying down.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: Um, so, would you say ultimately, it's better when you lie down? Or have you not ?
Patient: Uh, yeah, I would say so.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Paracetamol did not provide headache relief.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: Has that helped?
Patient: Um, not really, no.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports current work-related stress and a heavy workload.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Patient: Um, work's kind of, um, a bit stressful at the moment. I've got a lot going on.
Patient: Um, yeah, I just seem to have like, a lot of, kind of, a backlog of work that I need to go through at the moment. So, I've kind of, been, doing a lot of late nights as well.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Work stress has been ongoing for about two months.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: Right, OK. Um, and, um, how long has that been the case for?
Patient: Uh, for probably about a couple of months now.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Sometimes feels anxious at work due to panic about not meeting deadlines.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: , no, not necessarily at work, sometimes I do feel a bit anxious. Um, but I, I kind of just, uh, the panic of not being able to get my work done on time.

Doctor: Do you have any , have you had any thoughts about harming yourself or hurting yourself?
Patient: No.

Past_Medical_History.content: History of anxiety for about two years.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: Patient: Um, I've had, um, so I had, like anxiety for about, two years now, and I've been on, uh, Sertraline for, a while.

Doctor: OK. Um, do you have any other illnesses at all?
Patient: Uh, none.

Past_Medical_History.content: No history of diagnosed high blood pressure.
Past_Medical_History.source_text:
Doctor: Have you ever been diagnosed with high blood pressure?
Patient: No.

Past_Medical_History.content: Has never had blood pressure checked.
Past_Medical_History.source_text:
Doctor: Have you ever had your blood pressure checked?
Patient: No.

Medications.source_text:
Doctor: OK. Are you taking Sertraline at the moment?
Patient: Yes.

Medications.content: Took paracetamol this morning for the headache.
Medications.source_text: Patient: Um, I've taken some Paracetamol.

Medications.content: No other medications besides sertraline and today’s paracetamol.
Medications.source_text: Patient: Um, no, other, other than Sertraline and having taken, um, Paracetamol this morning, uh, nothing else.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text:
Doctor: Do you have any allergies to any medication?
Patient: Not that I'm aware of, no.

Family_History.source_text:
Doctor: can I just double-check, does anyone in your family have any migraines or anything like that? They've been diagnosed with migraines?
Patient: Uh, no. They haven't.

Family_History.content: Mother has a history of anxiety.
Family_History.source_text: Patient: My parents, uh, my mum's had a history of anxiety as well...

Family_History.content: No significant physical illnesses reported in the family.
Family_History.source_text: Patient: ...but, no kind of like physical illnesses or anything like that.

Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Patient: Um, I live with my partner.

Doctor: OK. Are you a smoker?
Patient: No.

Doctor: And, uh, do you have any pets at home?
Patient: Uh, I have a cat.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Runs at least three times a week.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Patient: Um, so normally I, try to go running at least three times a week.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Diet is average; not particularly healthy but not unhealthy.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text:
Patient: Um, it's OK, um, it's nothing, it's nothing um, really healthy, um, but it's fine.
Patient: I wouldn't say unhealthy.

Assessment.content: Tension-type headache is a diagnostic possibility.
Assessment.source_text: Doctor: But, um, it sounds like it might be one of two things. It could be an element of what we call tension headache.
Doctor: The other possibility is, um, migraine as well.

Assessment.content: Unilateral pain and light sensitivity increase the likelihood of migraine.
Assessment.source_text: Doctor: OK. Um, and, the fact, what makes that more likely is the fact that it's on one side, and that you've got some sensitivity to light.

Assessment.content: Work-related pressure and past anxiety increase the likelihood of a tension headache.
Assessment.source_text: Doctor: OK. That's one possibility. Um, and what makes that, more likely is the fact that, you've been under some pressure, and you have a history of anxiety in the past, OK.

Plan_of_Care.content: Start ibuprofen as first-line treatment for suspected migraine-type headache.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: So, um, the medication-wise, the things that we'd start off first line, if someone had migraine was to, would be to start Ibuprofen.

Plan_of_Care.content: Ibuprofen dosing may be higher than normal over-the-counter doses.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: And um, uh, that, the doses of Ibuprofen can be a bit, more than the normal doses Ibuprofen so that's one thing we can start.

Plan_of_Care.content: May continue paracetamol; ibuprofen is more effective for migraine.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: You can keep on taking Paracetamol as well if you like, but the, the Ibuprofen's um, actually more effective , for migraine.

Plan_of_Care.content: Guidelines now recommend ibuprofen or aspirin as first-line over paracetamol for migraine.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: And, um, yeah, so the, the guidelines have changed, recently we used, we, before that we used to give Paracetamol as first line but now it's, um, Ibuprofen or Aspirin.

Plan_of_Care.content: Consider taking time off work, potentially a week of self-certified leave, to reduce stress.
Plan_of_Care.source_text:
Doctor: That's, thing. Um, the other thing I'd like you to do, is maybe consider taking some time off work. OK, because if the headache is due to stress from work.
Doctor: Um, maybe having a week off if you self-certify, that might help with things.

Plan_of_Care.content: Explore counseling options and self-refer to local counseling service via provided link.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: And I'd also like you to explore, counselling options as well so there's, a counselling service in your area, that I can give you the link for, for you to self-refer.
Doctor: As well as those two things, other things I'd like you to do, is to try and ensure that you're having a minimum of seven, eight hours sleep at night, every night.

Plan_of_Care.content: Drink 1.5–2 liters of water or fluids daily, excluding coffee or tea.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: And you're drinking a minimum of, um, one point five to two litres uh, of water or fluids a day, and that's not including coffee or tea.

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient provided a link to headache danger signs to review for when to seek care.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: Um, and I'll also leave a link, to some of the danger signs of symptoms of headaches, in the notes. If you can read through that in your own time, that will just help you to have a bit more, control over what's going on and understanding of what, what, what kind of things, should trigger you contacting another doctor.

Plan_of_Care.content: If symptoms do not improve, consider arranging blood tests and evaluating other possibilities.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: OK. Um, and let's have a follow-up appointment, if we're finding that things are not getting better, we might need to arrange some blood tests or um, look at uh, other possibilities, but, we'll try that in the first instance.

Follow_up_Information.source_text: Doctor: I'd like you to, , OK I'd like you to try that. Um, what, we're gonna do is, we'll have a follow-up in a week's time.

Follow_up_Information.content: Advised to call back sooner if symptoms worsen or if concerned.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Doctor: Um, if anything changes in the meantime, or you get worried or things get worse. Feel free, have a lower threshold for ringing us back and we can book you an appointment, and we can reassess the situation.
